entry-web.description: Where the browser starts: the router, the document with its Splash for iOS, the offline page, and one thin route for each Place. The router reaches the routes through the generated route tree, so nothing imports them

entry-worker.description: Where the Worker starts: /rpc goes to the Remote Backend, everything else to the app

entry-infra.description: Deployable resources, composed by alchemy.run.ts: the D1 database, core's ledger table on it, and the Worker

client-screens.description: What the user sees in a browser: the shell around every Place, each Place, the sheets over them, and the parts they share

screens.description: The shell holds every sheet; each Place is its own module the routes open; all of them draw with the shared parts, and Entries opens the Account sheet too

client-app.description: Ledger's client from core, made once on the web platform Layer, with the theme: what every screen uses for Ledger's state, Settings, Users and Backend

client-platform.description: The web platform Layer core asks for: tables and Remote copies in IndexedDB, the last User in localStorage, Google sign-in through the Auth Worker's cookies, the Ledger API at this origin, and the window's network and visibility events

client-kit.description: What Ledger needed that no package has yet: sounds made on demand, the Thumb Picker, what the device can be driven by, and how keys read and are recorded on this platform. Each knows nothing of Ledger

server-remote.description: The Remote Backend's server half: core's Backend on D1, checked by the Auth Worker, answering /rpc over HTTP

ledger-web.description: Read top-down: entry starts the browser and the Worker; the screens over Ledger's client from core, made on the web platform Layer, and the web kit; the Worker over the Remote Backend's server half and the infra. Everything shared with the Expo app is in @ledger/core
